Long Haul

Ultra largo radio

A non-stop flight covering an exceptionally long distance, typically over 16 hours or more than 7,000 nautical miles, requiring special crew and operational procedures.

Questions and answers

Questions and answers

What is Ultra largo radio?

In this glossary, Ultra largo radio refers to: A non-stop flight covering an exceptionally long distance, typically over 16 hours or more than 7,000 nautical miles, requiring special crew and operational procedures.

How is Ultra largo radio used in aviation?

In aviation communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "La operación ultra largo radio requiere descanso anticipado de la tripulación y múltiples alternativos para planificación de contingencia."

Why does Ultra largo radio matter in aviation?

Ultra largo radio matters because it supports clear communication in Long Haul contexts for Pilots, Air Traffic Controllers, and Cabin Crew. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as ICAO Level 4, ICAO Level 5, ICAO Level 6, and EASA FCL.055.

Who uses Ultra largo radio?

Ultra largo radio is mainly used by Pilots, Air Traffic Controllers, and Cabin Crew.

What category does Ultra largo radio belong to?
